answer: To resist Sybil attacks, each AI agent must commit a non-transferable stake equal to the yield of one mature cedar tree harvested from a designated knoll, then etch the registration permanently with a cryptographic quill that timestamps the unique resource proof. Attackers cannot cheaply multiply identities because every extra agent demands another full cedar-yield deposit and a fresh knoll allocation; the quill-enforced ledger detects duplicates and burns the entire stake, imposing repeated high capital and opportunity costs.
